  "cut_point": "We are given the polynomial identity:

$$
(x^2 + 1)(x - 1)^8 = a_0 + a_1(x - 2) + a_2(x - 2)^2 + \cdots + a_{10}(x - 2)^{10}
$$

We are to find:

$$
a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10}
$$

---

### Step 1: Understand the structure

The left-hand side is a polynomial of degree 10 (since $(x^2 + 1)$ is degree 2, and $(x - 1)^8$ is degree 8, so their product is degree 10).

The right-hand side is a polynomial in terms of $(x - 2)$, expanded up to degree 10. So the expansion is a **Taylor polynomial** of the left-hand side around $x = 2$.

We want the **sum of the coefficients** from $a_1$ to $a_{10}$, which is the same as the value of the polynomial **evaluated at $x = 2$** **minus the constant term $a_0$**.",
  "reflection": {
    "verified_state": [
      "The left-hand side polynomial has degree 10.",
      "The right-hand side is the expansion of the polynomial in powers of (x-2), i.e. its Taylor polynomial around x=2."
    ],
    "error_step": "We want the **sum of the coefficients** from $a_1$ to $a_{10}$, which is the same as the value of the polynomial **evaluated at $x = 2$** **minus the constant term $a_0$**.",
    "error_reason": "Evaluating at x=2 gives only a0, so subtracting a0 gives 0, not a1+...+a10. In the (x-2)-basis, the sum of all coefficients is obtained by setting x-2=1, i.e. x=3.",
    "new_direction": "Evaluate P at x=3 to obtain a0+a1+...+a10, then subtract a0=P(2)=5 to find the required sum."
  }
